newsitem.title: UK: BRADFORD WOOL MARKET AGAIN QUIET DUE HOLIDAYS.
newsitem.headline: BRADFORD WOOL MARKET AGAIN QUIET DUE HOLIDAYS.

text.p: Some talk was heard of business being placed in the Far East but leading European markets were again quiet because of holidays.

Most interest was on Australia where the market confirmed signs of softness seen last week. The EMI ended 22 cents down on the week at 696 and noone was sure whether a recovery of one cent on Thursday marked the end of the shake out or a pause.

Prices to reflect the wool market have to be lower but sterling volatility involved erratic softness against the Australian dollar. Those importing tops were best placed because of the currency advantage. But a new UK interest rate rise did not trigger any further sterling appreciation.
